hints: Calculate the maximum friction on each block: $F_{A,\max} = 0.2(30) = 6\text{ N}$ and $F_{B,\max} = 0.3(50) = 15\text{ N}$.

In limiting equilibrium, block $A$ requires string tension $T = F_{A,\max} = 6\text{ N}$. For block $B$, the pull balances both the tension and friction: $P_{\max} = T + F_{B,\max} = 6 + 15 = 21\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the maximum static friction forces on blocks $A$ and $B$:
$$F_{A,\max} = \mu_A m_A g = 0.2(30) = 6\text{ N}$$
$$F_{B,\max} = \mu_B m_B g = 0.3(50) = 15\text{ N}$$

Analyze the equilibrium of block $A$ and the whole system:
- Equilibrium of block $A$:
$$T = F_{A,\max} = 6\text{ N}$$
- Equilibrium of the combined system:
$$P_{\max} = F_{A,\max} + F_{B,\max} = 6 + 15 = 21\text{ N}$$

- Block $A$ resists with $6\text{ N}$, and block $B$ resists with $15\text{ N}$:
$$F_A = 6\text{ N}, \quad F_B = 15\text{ N}$$

Sum resistances for the train:
- Total pull needed to budge both blocks is:
$$P_{\max} = 6 + 15 = 21\text{ N}$$
The string tension holding trailing block $A$ is $6\text{ N}$.
